# Motion VAE

This module contains the checkpoint-compatible causal body/hand VAE and a
standalone training and inference pipeline. It consumes normalized 333D SMPL-X
features: translation (3), body rotations (150), and two hands (90 each).
The latent has 256 channels and a temporal stride of three.

The training objective retains the original optimal-sigma Gaussian reconstruction
NLL, KL divergence, and a root NLL over the first nine channels, weighted by 7.
The default architecture and AdamW settings are in `configs/motion_vae.yaml`.
The standalone scripts omit text evaluators, word vectors, experiment-service
dependencies, and machine-specific launchers.

Install a PyTorch build suitable for your device, then install the remaining
dependencies with `pip install -r third_party/motion_vae/requirements.txt`.
See the standalone Motion VAE section in the root README for commands.

Weights, datasets, training logs, and generated outputs are not bundled.
`--checkpoint` accepts the original `{"net": state_dict}` checkpoint format or a
plain state dictionary. Training can start from scratch or warm-start from these
weights; a warm start creates a new optimizer rather than resuming optimizer state.
Checkpoints generated by the standalone trainer retain the `net` key used by the
DuoFlow preprocessing and inference helpers.

`assets/motion_vae_stats/mean.npy` and `std.npy` contain the normalization used
by the released 333D pipeline. Use matching statistics when training a new model.
The encoder samples the posterior even in evaluation mode, matching the original
model. The inference CLI sets a seed for reproducibility.
